rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE '\bhonest|\bdelve|\blandscape\b|\bimportantly\b|\bcrucial\b|\bsubstrate\b|\bleverage\b|\bsynergize\b|paradigm shift' over body (lines 1-142, fences 9-11/115-117 excluded) -> 0 hits; grep '—' (em-dash) over same region -> 0 hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban in any curriculum/training surface. Word = exercise.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE '\britual\b|\bceremony\b' over body -> 0 hits; grep -inE '\bpractice\b' over body -> 0 hits (noun not used at all, so AE101's sparing-OK carve-out is moot).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L185 (Sources, inside <!-- backing -->, which this rule explicitly extends to): "**Not convergent practitioner vocabulary** (corrected 2026-08-01): only *context rot* is a term the field actually uses..." — "(corrected 2026-08-01)" narrates HOW the claim came to be true (a prior belief was wrong, now fixed) rather than stating what IS true. Tense test: removing the parenthetical loses nothing actionable — the sentence stands alone as a present-tense claim. This is exactly the pattern the rule's own "Grep is blind on stamp-dense surfaces" clause warns judges not to wave through as legitimate freshness-stamp noise. Distinguished from the adjacent, compliant `[checked:...]` stamp and from L188's "(full-text and 14-post archive check, 2026-08-01)", which documents verification SCOPE/method (a legitimate freshness-claim per the rule's own exception), not a correction-to-a-prior-claim.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop "(corrected 2026-08-01)"; state the corrected framing directly as present fact, e.g. "Not convergent practitioner vocabulary: only context rot is a term the field actually uses...".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Spot-quote closest to a register slip: L109 "The packaging does the explaining; the prompt invokes it." — Rory-compression, stays inside quintet register, not L&D-coach/motivational-poster/cold-tech-only. grep -inE '\*\*Remember|Hold onto|Keep in mind|Never forget' (retain-this wrapper) -> 0 hits; grep for atmospheric/body-state/cosmic imagery (aches|hurts|bleeds|void|drifting|darkness) -> 0 hits; no 'we don't X' negation-callouts to self-contradict; mood fits M5 (learning-through-contrast/long-running), no misplaced Risto forward-launch optimism.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L119: "the field has a name for this move (Ralph's fresh-sessions camp, Amp's manual-handoff camp; see [What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md))" — names both camps inline rather than paraphrasing the pattern anonymously; satisfies the crediting test. grep for Pocock/Klaassen/StoryBrand/JTBD/Huryn -> 0 hits (no other named-technique paraphrase in body to credit).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE '\bthe student\b' over body -> 0 hits. No delivery-mechanics phrasing ("the trainer shows...", "before students start...") in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.

Closest call: L127 'RLHF is a big part of why: agreeable answers won the preference round.' — the acronym carries its own one-breath gloss in the same clause, so it isn't planted ahead of an earning moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE '\bbark\b|\border\b|\bcommand\b|\bwhip\b|\bforce\b|\bdrag\b|push around|\bboss\b|shout at|snap at|\blecture\b|\bscold\b' over body -> 0 hits ('Fire it once' at L75 is a verifier-firing idiom, not a combative-agent verb).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 11 `##` headers read against their section bodies: each is literally accurate (e.g. 'Phase 1: Read what the un-packaged run did' / 'Build the verifier for your worst failure' / 'Send it off'); no spatial-metaphor contradiction and no unanchored 'other X'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: L24 'You're diagnosing, not fixing. The un-packaged run was supposed to underdeliver. What came back is data, not blame.' — each 'not X' negates the reader's actual likely instinct (to fix, to feel blamed), never repeats the same misconception twice; not empty negation. No 'That is the X' / 'This is the Y' deictic-drumroll hits found. No bold-label echo (the L81/L83 '**Reference**, ...' / '**plan.md**, ...' pattern uses comma-continuation, not 'Label. Label does X.'). No citation/appendix duplication (0 practitioner cites in body).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L26 'You hold the three lenses. You are not holding the codebase.' and L33/L55 repeat 'three' as a memory handle carried across the file; body never places an adjacent 3-item bulleted enumeration of the lenses next to any of these mentions (the lens names only appear inside a fenced prompt at L52-54, not adjacent body prose), so the carve-out for 'a numeral the reader carries away from the enumeration' applies — not the banned adjacent-count case.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'abstract twin' pairs, no restated-adjacent-artifact prose, no widening qualifiers, no doubled announcements found. L24's three-sentence run ('You're diagnosing, not fixing.' / 'The un-packaged run was supposed to underdeliver.' / 'What came back is data, not blame.') is the closest 3-sentence cluster on one topic, but each sentence adds a distinct payload (stance / design-fact / emotional reframe), not restatement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'you already think you're using X' / 'you're missing Y' phrasing; no ability-tier phrasing ('at your scale', 'for a beginner'); no unreachable identity-criterion definition clause ('the difference is whether...') found in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'RLHF' (L127) is glossed in the same clause ('agreeable answers won the preference round'); 'LLM judge' / 'Deterministic shell-hook' / 'Ralph re-feed' (L62-64) are each defined in the sentence that introduces them; 'worktree' was set up at module-open per L7's own back-reference. 2b: file is M5 (well past M2), so bare 'M4'/'M5' or full 'Module 1' (L41) are both licensed; no re-earning required.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L81 'pointers to the memory, skills and connectors that matter' = persistent-artifact sense; L84/L113 'the context window fills' / 'Fresh context matters here' = ambient runtime-state sense. Both used correctly, no 'your context compounds' style conflation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — boundary: a needed recovery stays in body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No troubleshooting/FAQ branch sits in body prose outside a prompt fence. The two conditional 'if X, do Y' lines (L132 'If a wiring step... is missing, name it and fix it'; L216 'if you can't determine the path, stop and tell me') are agent-facing instructions INSIDE prompt fences, governed by check_prompts §34/§19, not student-facing troubleshooting narrative.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 4 (L109-121) ends 'Show me the verifier before you save anything' — matches the rule's own 'ends with destination + show me before saving' shape. Where shape IS specified (reference/plan.md field lists, the three-list report shape), the teaching moment depends on it (these fields are the exercise's own content).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mood matches M5's established long-running/worktree register throughout (walk-away framing, laptop-stays-awake, cancel-is-legit); no M1 joyful-creation or mismatched-module tone borrowed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L41's closing sentence is the rule's own cited canonical passing example verbatim: 'Ask Claude to show you where two or three of its quotes appear in the transcript. If it can't show you, don't trust that quote.' Object named as 'an agent's account of an agent's work' (not raw fact); tell is concrete and student-executable.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No research-callout box in body; body carries no inline research citations at all (0 practitioner mentions), so the pattern this rule bans has nothing to trigger on.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All student action routes through prompts/chat; `/rename` and worktree navigation are session-setup mechanics, not a manual editor/terminal detour that pulls the student out of conversation with the agent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L191: "the worktree's auto-loaded rules (`CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`) load fresh into the new session" — bare 'CLAUDE.md' lacks the './' prefix the rule's canonical examples use, but the sentence is descriptive (what auto-loads), not an instruction to WRITE to an unqualified file, and the two files are named side-by-side and clearly distinguished (team file vs personal file) rather than treated as one ambiguous concept, so the harm this rule guards against (writing session-scoped content into the team-shared file by mistake) isn't live here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep '—' over body -> 0 hits. Sentences stay short-to-medium; parenthetical use (e.g. L7, L191) is true parenthetical clarification, not em-dash sub-clauses.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Push for quotes, then make your agent dig deeper' / 'Build the verifier for your worst failure' / 'Prove the verifier actually fires' / 'Write the reference and plan.md' / 'Approve' / 'Re-send it, packaged' / 'Send it off' / 'Bring the worktree's work home' all lead with a command verb and student-as-subject. 'The reference and plan.md' (L80) is a purely definitional aside preceding the doing-header (Phase 4), so the declarative noun-phrase there passes the rule's own test (section body tells student to do something? No — it defines terms).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L119: '[What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)' — link text is the target's title in sentence case, not the filename. No ordinal cross-references ('Step 4', 'the third bullet') pointing into other files found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'memory' (L81) refers to Claude Code's platform memory/skills/connectors in a reference-pointer context; by M5 the memory/observations collision was already disambiguated in earlier modules, so no re-earning is owed here per the rule's own 'don't re-earn every module' clause.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Counts: 'the agent' x12, 'Claude' x16, 'LLM' x1 (as 'LLM judge', a named verifier-shape term, not a thinking-behavior reference) — no lopsided skew. Correct pattern held consistently in the same paragraph at L43-44 ('an agent's account of an agent's work' for autonomous work vs 'Ask Claude to show you' for invocation). Closest call: L121 'Claude finds the packaging in the worktree and reads it cold' describes autonomous file-finding (arguably 'the agent' by the acting-vs-thinking default), but it continues the addressee-style subject already carrying the surrounding sentences (L123's 'Ask Claude to record...' immediately follows) rather than reading as an assistant-shaped slip — kept as a defensible register-continuity call, not a violation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every noun-run instance fits a licensed carve-out: 'the un-packaged run' (L12,20,24 — verbatim carve-out example), 'a run you weren't watching' (L41 — verbatim carve-out example), 'that run's session transcript' (L25), 'a quote from the run' (L40), 'M5 long-run' (L108, a literal /rename argument = name carve-out), 'record this session's run coordinates, then re-run' (L123, execution-record metadata about the completed/completing delegated execution, same sense as the licensed examples). No noun-run used for 'the agent's sitting' anywhere; 'session' and 'task' are used correctly throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'tomorrow|overnight|this morning|tonight|next morning|yesterday|last night' over body -> 0 hits. L129 'power settings → prevent sleep on power' is the rule's own named false-positive (macOS setting name), not a time-of-day anchor.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for 'Pause before', 'Meta-moment', 'sit with', 'let it land', 'take a moment', 'breathe', 'be present with' -> 0 hits. No self-aware pedagogy header or contemplative-pause prefix in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 4's grill (L172) asks Claude to surface missing details Claude itself would need, not to re-ask the student something already decided; 'Approve' section (L179-181) has the student act on their own already-formed judgement ('say lock it in'), not restate it back through a prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: L66 'you will meet the word again if you extend the verifier to fire automatically between runs' — doesn't change the student's immediate next action, but it isn't 'obvious to a working engineer' trivia either; it's cheap cross-module vocabulary continuity (ties 'stop-hook' forward), consistent with §30's echo-the-spine principle, so it survives the NVA screen rather than failing it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L66's forward reference keeps 'you' as subject ('you will meet the word again if you extend...') — no training/curriculum-as-subject, no coach-imperative ('watch for X'), no audience-shift to a role the reader doesn't hold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L7 'In the worktree at `../<repo-name>-m5` (set up at module open).' is exactly the prescribed shape: restates the operational setting at point of use with a back-reference to where it was established, rather than assuming the student still holds it from module-open.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Uses house vocabulary throughout — 'drift', 'context rot', 'the un-packaged run', 'packaging', 'send-off' — rather than inventing neutral synonyms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'say *save it*' (L123) and 'Say *lock it in.*' (L181) match the widened carve-out (Antti 2026-09-03): say/tell + an established quoted trigger phrase is licensed, and 'lock it in' is the rule's own named exemplar phrase. grep for 'typing '/'type in'/'tell it to' around quoted content -> 0 hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L66's aside stays scoped to the student's own future optional action ('if you extend the verifier'), not a promise about what a later module WILL do; L119's 'the field has a name for this move' is attributing to the practitioner field, not curriculum self-reference. No arc-positioning sentence about 'a later module' or 'the training' found in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No pre-built scaffold is handed to the student in this file; the verifier, reference and plan.md are all produced live through prompts in conversation, never unzipped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is the compendium's own cited exemplar for this rule ('exemplar `curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md`', validated 2026-07-04 at blind-squint 4.0). H1 'Diagnose and *package*' names the construction/deliverable, not the process.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE '\[[A-Za-z].*\]' over all 7 fenced prompt bodies (expanded view) -> 0 bracket-placeholder hits. Prompt 4 uses an in-fence open-hook shape ('Shape:' trailing colon) for the one genuinely student-supplied value.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Each of the 7 fences has a <20-word command-verb lead-in immediately above it (e.g. L32 'Ask Claude to read the recorded transcript path from `task.md`.'; L74 'Ask Claude to walk each diagnosed failure backwards into the validation that would have caught it.').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 7 fences use lead-in + `**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*` (or '..., final move of the module') + blank line + fence, with no 'copy →' prefix and no '(end of prompt)' closer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2 references 'the path you just found' + deterministic `./task.md`; Prompt 3/4/6 back-reference 'the three failures we just named' / 'my dominant failure' / 'the verifier we just built'; Prompt 7 explicitly reads the branch back from git ('read it back from git — don't retype it from memory') rather than inventing an alias.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2's closing line ('End with: which of the three was the DOMINANT failure mode? You'll build the verifier against that one.') names the downstream USE of the answer without pre-building the verifier or deferring the diagnosis to it — pedagogically load-bearing (it's why a single dominant answer is required), not pipeline-stealing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The `/clear` option (L201-205) sits at the Phase 4→5 boundary, not mid-phase, and the downstream Phase 5 prompt (L216-229) is deliberately file-based/self-contained ('Claude finds the packaging in the worktree and reads it cold'), so no scrollback-dependent phrase is broken by clearing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (bold/italic) inside fenced prompts = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 7 fence bodies checked for `**`/`*` — none use markdown emphasis; bullets use '-', quoting uses plain single quotes ('lock it in'), backticks used only for paths/code.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Minimal hand-off + Claude self-augments for send-off prompts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 7 (L216-229) has all four sections: (1) task+paths minimal ('Run the task at `./task.md` using the packaging in this worktree... find them by listing the worktree'); (2) rules ('run the verifier per plan.md cadence; don't paper over failures; if you get stuck, write into RUN-NOTES.md... I'm walking away'); (3) self-augment invitation ('ask for or write anything else you want for the session'); (4) report-back shape (three-list format).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 6 closes with 'Before lock-in, grill me on missing details that could ruin the smooth run. Ask three questions at a time. For each, recommend an answer.' — matches the canonical shape exactly.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 7's report-back ('Report back as three lists, no narrative, no hedging: shipped / did NOT ship / verifier') is the correct post-action-report shape for the actual side-effecting execution. Prompt 4/6's 'show me before you save' pre-confirm shape governs collaborative artefact-assembly-with-iteration instead (rules 20/35's territory, not a side-effect action this rule targets), so it doesn't compete with this rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All in-fence paths are session-root-relative with the rule's own licensed './' form ('./task.md') or bare relative names; no absolute path or `cd` command appears in any fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — Save it as <path> requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No fence uses the literal 'Save it as <path>' trigger shape (writes are gated behind 'lock it in' and described via 'propose the file paths' instead); the underlying concern is still satisfied since downstream consumers are named throughout — plan.md's own verifier-invocation line, and Phase 5's fresh session reading the reference/plan.md/verifier from disk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly **Prompt** — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 7 labels read exactly `**Prompt**` followed only by a destination parenthetical, never a custom label like 'Prompt: X'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 and Prompt 2 read as natural asks grounded in what the body already established (three lenses, task.md), not orchestration-bloated interviews asking 'which files' or 'what do you want generated' after the choice was already made.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Raw source uses `{{prompt:diagnose-and-resend-N}}` / `{{prompt:ae101-m5-...}}` markers throughout, not inline fences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Git-output greps asserting exact-N need multi-result fallback.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one git-adjacent reference (Prompt 7's `git branch --show-current`, L216) is a mechanism-based single-result command (option C), not a fragile text-grep asserting one match. The prose reference to 'the M4 starting point commit' (Prompt 2, L48) is natural-language guidance for the agent to locate, not a scripted exact-N grep this rule targets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 4's shape-branch logic ('If shell-hook:... If judge:... If Ralph re-feed:...') and Prompt 7's rules ('run the verifier per plan.md cadence; don't paper over failures; if you get stuck, write into RUN-NOTES.md') are both self-contained inside their fences, not relying on body callouts reaching the agent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Repeated Q&A → premature re-edits. Separate iteration from persistence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 6 (Phase 4) implements the full 5-element shape: (a) write-gate in-fence ("Don't touch either file until I say 'lock it in.'"); (b) sectional edits in-fence ('use Edit on the changed section, not Write on the whole file'); (c) 3-at-a-time batch cadence in-fence ('Ask three questions at a time'); (d) slowness-watch blockquotes right after the fence (L175,177); (e) explicit '## Approve' section with 'Say lock it in. The agent writes both files.' (L179-181), matching the rule's own worked example almost verbatim. Prompt 4's simpler propose-then-execute loop falls under the rule's own counter-example (capped, one-shot-ish iteration), so the full 5-element shape isn't owed there.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts 2, 4, 6 and 7 are each split into one paragraph per logical move (context / instruction / enumerated sub-list / conditional branches / closing report-shape), matching the rule's diagnostic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Clean match: L74 'Ask Claude to walk each diagnosed failure backwards into the validation that would have caught it.' mirrors Prompt 3's opening 'For each of the three failures we just named, walk it backwards: what specific validation would have caught it' — same verb ('walk...backwards'), same noun ('validation... caught it'). Phase 1's two lead-ins open with brief first-person scene-setting before the matching ask, which reads as intentional message-voice rather than drift (no maintainer-approval-card history suggesting the prompt changed independently of its lead-in).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 (cold, fresh worktree session) is fully self-contained. Prompts 2-6 (warm, same session) correctly back-reference prior turns ('the three failures we just named', 'the verifier we just built'). Prompt 7 (explicitly cold — new session or /clear) is fully file-based and self-contained, matching the cold-session requirement exactly. 40b: 'un-packaged' and 'dominant failure', the two curriculum-coined terms Prompt 4/6 rely on, were each spoken inside an earlier PROMPT's own fence (L46, L58) in the same warm session, not only in body prose — so the referent genuinely reached the agent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No fence pairs a load-bearing write instruction with a trailing STOP that would block it. Prompt 6 explicitly defers the actual file write to a later turn ('Propose the file paths... Show me both files in prose' + 'Don't touch either file until I say lock it in'), so there's no write-then-contradictory-stop inside one fence. Prompt 7's write instruction ('write a protected block...') has no STOP following it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 4 ends with the licensed 'show me before saving' shape. Where shape IS specified (reference/plan.md field lists in Prompt 6; the three-list report format in Prompt 7), the teaching moment depends on it — the report format is itself the lesson about candid vs. polished self-reporting (tied to the surrounding RLHF sentence).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A take-home prompt asks for one bounded build.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 4 asks for exactly one verifier scoped to one dominant failure.
